title: Who Is Indigenous? The Politics of Tribal Identity Terminology in India and Bangladesh
author: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
text:
Dancers and drummers of the Kurukh Oraon Adivasi community of eastern India.
Credit: Wikipedia/Rocky International
On August 9, the government in the eastern Indian state of West Bengal did not host events marking the International Day of the World’s Indigenous Peoples. Last year, the day was celebrated with events across the state over four days. The new Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government that came to power in May issued a notice on August 5, stating that this year’s celebration was cancelled. No reason was given for the decision.West Bengal’s indigenous people’s organizations protested the move, as did the opposition parties. “This is an assault on the indigenous people’s identity and pride,” Mayukh Biswas, a leader of the West Bengal unit of the Communist Party of India-Marxists, said, alleging that the decision stemmed from the BJP’s ideological project of denying the adivasi (indigenous/aboriginal) identity of the tribal population.[...]
